articles.title: Bold College Fantasy Football Predictions for Week 9
articles.summary: College fantasy football analysts Eric Froton and Nick Bromberg get bold for Week 9.
articles.body:
Yahoo Sports College Football analysts Eric Froton and Nick Bromberg reveal their boldest predictions for Week 9 of the CFF season.

Nolan James Jr. runs for 100+ yards and a score

While Aneyas Williams was considered the opening day starting running back for the Irish, his inability to grind out yardage on the interior opened the door for challengers. James has shown the ability to consistently create extra yardage, averaging 3.64 yards after contact while Williams is at 2.29 YAC with a disappointing 4.32 yards per carry.

James fully took over the room versus BYU last week, rushing 16 times for 77 yards while scoring 10+ fantasy points in all seven games this season. I think James clears the century mark with a score this weekend against Navy and emphatically lays claim to the starting job for the rest of the season. — Froton

Missouri QB Austin Simmons throws for 300+ yards, 3 TDs against Arkansas

The Tigers took their lumps in a 31-3 loss to Ole Miss last game, but they've been a steamroller against the rest of their schedule, scoring at least 24+ points in their other six games while ranking 15th nationally with 24% of completions gaining 20+ yards. Simmons has competently led this aggressive passing attack that averages 10.5 of target depth per pass (11th) and 16.3 yards per successful dropback (24th).

He has the advantage of facing a beleaguered Arkansas defense that is still finding its footing under new HC Ryan Silverfield, ranking 126th in yards per successful dropback and 109th in yards per drive. I think Missouri gets back on track in style, as Simmons leads the way with 300+ yards and 3+ touchdowns. — Froton

The Duke RB has been one of the most productive running backs in college fantasy football thanks to his touchdown production. He's scored 13 TDs and has found the end zone in every game.

However, he hasn't cracked the 100-yard rushing mark since he had nine carries for 116 yards against William & Mary in Week 4. He's made up for that with his receiving ability — Sheppard had 91 receiving yards against Georgia Tech and then 11 catches for 98 yards against North Carolina — but is in line to finally cross the century mark again on Saturday. Boston College is allowing over 150 rushing yards per game. — Bromberg

Pitt's Cataurus Hicks will continue to thrive despite QB uncertainty

Pitt's season has gone south ever since QB Mason Heintschel suffered a season-ending knee injury against Virginia Tech. But the Panthers' subsequent struggles at quarterback — and on offense in general — haven't deterred Hicks' fantasy relevance.

Hicks has scored at least 19 points in three of the last four weeks. He had five catches for 149 yards and a score last week against Miami after grabbing five passes for 135 yards and a TD the week before against Boston College. And Georgia Tech, Hicks' next opponent, is all out of sorts this year.

Hicks is available in over 70% of leagues. There are far worse options available if you're in need of a receiver. — Bromberg

articles.summary: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf have built a marriage that has lasted through fame, personal struggles and the pressures of professional sport.
articles.body: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf have built a marriage that has lasted through fame, personal struggles and the pressures of professional sport. When the tennis legends celebrated their 24th wedding anniversary in October 2025, their relationship drew renewed attention. Behind their long-standing bond, however, lies a story of difficult moments, emotional challenges and the steady support that helped them stay together. Agassi has often credited his wife with bringing stability to his life, while people close to the couple have described their relationship as strong but far from perfect.Andre Agassi credited Steffi Graf for changing his lifeLast year, Agassi marked their anniversary with a heartfelt message on social media, writing, “24 years with this wonderful woman. Happy Anniversary Steffi, you are my unicorn!”According to a source quoted by Heat, Graf played a significant role in helping Agassi maintain the stability he needed after overcoming his past struggles with substance use. The insider said Agassi had already stopped using drugs before their relationship began in 1999, but credited his wife with helping him remain on track.“Without Steffi by his side things could have turned out very differently for Andre, everyone that knows him would agree that she’s been a great influence on his life.”The couple married in a private ceremony, choosing jeans and bare feet instead of a traditional wedding celebration. They welcomed their son Jaden shortly afterwards and later had their daughter Jaz.Despite their sporting achievements, the couple chose to raise their children away from the pressure of professional tennis. Their son pursued baseball, while their daughter developed interests in dance and horseback riding.Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf's marriage faced its share of strugglesTheir relationship has not been without disagreements. The same insider told Heat that the tennis legends experience arguments and difficult periods like other couples.“It’s not always a bed of roses, they’re still human,” the source said.The insider added that Agassi sometimes struggles with his emotions, while Graf's calm personality helps keep their family grounded.Away from the spotlight, the couple have built a quiet life in Las Vegas. Both reportedly prefer spending time at home with their children and a small circle of friends rather than attending celebrity events.Interestingly, their home does not display their Grand Slam trophies. Graf once revealed, “We only have our children's trophies. Jaden from baseball and Jaz from hip-hop dancing.”As their children grow older, the former champions have found more time for their shared interests. They still play tennis together for fun, while Agassi has also embraced pickleball and made his professional debut in 2025.Their marriage may have faced difficult moments, but their shared values, family life and mutual support have remained central to their relationship.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Could Bryce Underwood Have a Future at Michigan Playing a Different Position?
articles.summary: With Tommy Carr taking over at quarterback and Bryce Underwood's future under center suddenly uncertain, could Michigan find another way to utilize the forme...
articles.body:
When Bryce Underwood arrived at Michigan , the expectation was that he would become the next great Wolverine quarterback. Now, less than a full season into the Kyle Whittingham era, it's fair to wonder whether his future in Ann Arbor might involve playing an entirely different position.

It sounds crazy considering Underwood's recruiting pedigree, but it's at least a conversation worth having.

Underwood was benched at halftime against Penn State after completing just five of 11 passes for 43 yards and two interceptions. True freshman Tommy Carr replaced him, led Michigan to a 21-18 victory and subsequently earned the starting assignment against Indiana.

Suddenly, Underwood's path back onto the field looks considerably more complicated, and maybe even impossible.

But here's the thing: Underwood is still one of the most physically gifted athletes on Michigan's roster.

At 6-4 and roughly 230 pounds, Underwood possesses a rare combination of size, speed and explosiveness. Even when he's struggled throwing the football, his ability to make defenders miss and generate yards with his legs has been obvious.

So why not find another way to get him involved?

The most intriguing possibility would be some sort of hybrid offensive role. Underwood could line up in the backfield alongside Carr, take direct snaps in short-yardage situations or even operate as a running threat on designed packages. Coincidentally, Whittingham's old program, Utah, is utilizing a two-QB system to perfection this year.

Essentially, Michigan could use him as an offensive weapon without asking him to shoulder the responsibilities of a traditional quarterback.

There's also the possibility of experimenting with Underwood at wide receiver or tight end, although those transitions would be considerably more complicated. Being a tremendous athlete doesn't automatically translate to running precise routes, catching passes in traffic or understanding blocking assignments. Underwood has been a pass catcher sparingly during his high school 7-on-7 days, but playing one of those positions at a place like Michigan in the Big Ten is a completely different animal.

And then there's the biggest obstacle of all: Would Underwood even entertain the idea?

He came to Michigan to play quarterback as THE No. 1 signal caller in the nation, and changing positions would represent a massive departure from the expectations surrounding his arrival. With the transfer portal providing opportunities elsewhere, there's no guarantee he'd be interested in reinventing himself.

It's also important to remember that Underwood is still quite young. Struggling as a quarterback early in his career doesn't mean he can't eventually develop into an excellent one. After all, his physical gifts are off the charts and it still feels like he could be unleashed with some different parameters.

Michigan shouldn't abandon that possibility simply because Carr has provided a spark.

Still, Whittingham and offensive coordinator Jason Beck desperately need more explosive playmakers, and Underwood's abilities are difficult to ignore.

Nobody is suggesting Michigan has actually approached Underwood about changing positions. But if Carr establishes himself as the long-term answer at quarterback, the Wolverines could eventually face an interesting decision.

Do they leave one of their most talented athletes standing on the sideline, or get creative enough to put him on the field?

It's an unconventional idea, but given Michigan's offensive struggles, perhaps it's one worth exploring.

articles.title: Joey Logano losing touch of his fourth Cup championship in 2026
articles.summary: Joey Logano is losing touch of a potential fourth NASCAR Cup Series championship after Talladega Superspeedway in 2026.
articles.body:
Joey Logano's pursuit of another NASCAR Cup Series championship suffered a significant setback during Sunday's YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway. The Team Penske driver started 16th, led 23 laps and won Stage 2 before a violent accident ended his afternoon in 34th place.

Logano displayed competitive speed throughout the second half of the event, repeatedly exchanging the lead with Ricky Stenhouse Jr. during the closing stages. His strongest moment came in Stage 2 when he narrowly defeated Kyle Larson for the stage victory by just 0.012 seconds.

However, his afternoon ended dramatically on Lap 183 when contact from Carson Hocevar destabilized his Ford in the outside drafting lane. Logano spun into traffic, and his car overturned during the ensuing 15-car accident.

The No. 22 Ford came to rest upside down before safety crews returned it to its wheels, allowing Logano to exit. The damage prevented him from continuing, leaving him 34th after 183 laps.

Logano earned 15 points and climbed one position to fifth in the Chase standings with 2,341 points. However, he now trails championship leader Kyle Larson by 100 points. Logano remains mathematically eligible for the title but will need substantial gains during the final two races.

articles.title: Young RBs fuel Sheridan in revenge win vs. Tri-Valley
articles.summary: Sheridan's young running backs carried a heavy load in a Division III, Region 11 playoff clash with Tri-Valley.
articles.body:
Sheridan pulls away from Philo, stays atop MVL-Big, top photos

THORNVILLE — Sophomore S.J. Shriner and freshman Emmitt Gilder have shined in Sheridan's backfield in Logan Russell's absence.

Their efforts were vital again on Friday night at Paul Culver Jr. Stadium, combining for more than 280 yards as a senior-laden offensive line paved the way in the sixth-seeded Generals' 38-35 triumph against No. 11-seed Tri-Valley in the Division III, Region 11 playoffs.

Shriner scored three times, including on a 9-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth quarter, while Gilder had game-sealing runs of 28 and 25 yards in the closing minutes of the final stanza. Sheridan remained unbeaten at home in playoff games.

The Generals (11-0) ended a five-game losing streak to the Scotties and avenged a 38-21 loss to them in Week 9 of the regular season. They travel to third seed Columbus East (9-1) in the quarterfinals at 7 p.m. on Nov. 6; that winner plays either No. 2 seed Licking Valley or No. 7 Granville in the semifinals.

Sheridan coach Paul Culver III praised his young running backs, while complimenting his five seniors on the offensive line, especially Milo Bullock.

"We told Milo we were going to run behind him on that final drive, and he led the way," Culver III said. "Our line did the job all night. Those two ran hard behind them, and Emmit could have scored late, but he had the intelligence to go down so we could take a knee and seal it.

"This win is for the 26 seniors, who mean so much to me, this community and school and to each other," he added. "I've been through a lot the past few weeks, and they've carried me. We talked about standing in the gap coming into this game, and they did that. They deserve this win."

Sheridan led 17-14 at the half on Liam Gutridge's 28-yard field goal right before the half.

The Generals took control in the third. Carson Harris scored on a 17-yard run to open the second-half scoring. After TJ Connors intercepted Tri-Valley's Stone Spiker on the ensuing possession, Logan Russell converted the takeaway into points with a 4-yard burst, making it 31-14 with three minutes left in the third.

However, the Scotties did not go quietly.

Leevi Wade, who ran for a school-record 362 yards in their regular season meeeting, capped the ensuing Tri-Valley drive with a 2-yard TD dive. After forcing a Sheridan punt, Spiker found top receiver Lucca Gargasz for a 79-yard scoring strike, which pulled the Scotties within 31-28 with 10 minutes left in the game.

Sheridan extended its lead on the next drive, as Shriner weaved 10 yards to the end zone, while Tri-Valley came back, as Spiker hit Logan Clapper for a 4-yard TD with four minutes left.

Despite Tri-Valley's rally falling short, coach Austin Jones never lost faith in his squad.

"They have super talented running backs and they're good up front," Jones said. "We also missed some tackles on the boundary. People doubted us coming into the season, and we could have packed it in at 3-3. But, our guys strapped it up and went to work to reach this point. Our seniors laid a good foundation for this program, and I know it's not easy after a game like this, but I'm proud what this group accomplished."

Shriner finished with 173 yards and three touchdowns, including scoring runs of 15 and 10 yards in the first quarter. Gilder added 108 yards on nine totes, and Tyce Whiteman was 10-of-16 passing for 111 yards with 38 yards on five carries for Sheridan.

Wade was held to 93 yards on 21 carries with three scores, including first-half TD runs of 1 yard in the first quarter and 2 yards in the second, and Spiker went 12-of-15 through the air for 209 yards to go with 42 yards on four rushes.

"Tri-Valley changed their identity, and hats off to their coaches for making that change so quickly," Culver III said. "That forced us to raise the bar. Our defensive coaches put in a great game plan and made good adjustments. I'm proud that our guys responded, and we get another week together."

articles.title: Thunder’s Injury Nightmare Could Have a Silver Lining for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
articles.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder watched as injuries piled up, turning an encouraging start into a difficult stretch for a team with championship expectations. Befo...
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder watched as injuries piled up, turning an encouraging start into a difficult stretch for a team with championship expectations. Before discussing standings or individual awards, the priority remains the players facing recovery and the teammates processing what happened.

Jalen Williams suffered a fractured left fibula and dislocated left ankle against the Los Angeles Clippers. Cason Wallace sustained a torn labrum in his left shoulder during that game. General manager Sam Presti announced that both players would require surgery, with return timelines to be determined afterward.

Jaylin Williams also exited that game with right wrist soreness, although he was subsequently cleared to play against Phoenix. That distinction matters. His situation should not be grouped with the extended absences facing Jalen Williams and Wallace.

For Oklahoma City, replacing their contributions will require more than shifting minutes around. Losing a secondary creator and a perimeter defender changes how the Thunder can attack opponents, protect leads and distribute responsibility throughout games.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander Faces a Different Challenge

The weight now falls more heavily on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, even with Oklahoma City needing contributions throughout its roster. The two-time MVP already commands defensive attention. Without Williams beside him, opponents have another reason to load up against his drives and force somebody else to create.

That could mean more scoring opportunities, but it also means tougher possessions. Additional shots do not automatically produce better basketball. Gilgeous-Alexander will need to balance aggression with trusting teammates, particularly when defenses try to turn every trip into a difficult individual assignment.

This is where his leadership becomes just as important as his production. Oklahoma City needs its best player to provide stability while others adjust to responsibilities they might not have anticipated carrying so early.

Another MVP Case Would Have to Be Earned

Before these injuries, a third consecutive MVP might have felt difficult to imagine. Voter fatigue can become part of the conversation when somebody keeps winning, and another excellent season might struggle to feel different from the previous two.

However, there is an argument available if Gilgeous-Alexander meets this challenge.

If he keeps Oklahoma City among the Western Conference's elite while increasing his production, voters would have a different situation to evaluate. Maintaining that standard without key teammates would provide evidence of his value beyond the numbers themselves.

That is a major if. The Thunder still need reliable shooting, defensive execution and enough contributions around him to win consistently. A scoring increase attached to a slide down the standings would make a less convincing argument.

Efficiency matters, too. Bigger numbers would carry more weight if Gilgeous-Alexander produces them without sacrificing the decision-making that makes him so effective.

Nobody should describe his teammates' injuries as good fortune. Their health comes first, and Oklahoma City's championship hopes are stronger with them available.

But if Gilgeous-Alexander helps hold this team together, keeps it competing near the top of the West and elevates his own play, dismissing another MVP case simply because he already has two would become difficult to justify.

articles.title: No one can stop Heat’s Giannis Antetokounmpo on tough and-1 vs. Pacers
articles.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo continues to exert brute force with an incredible highlight during the Miami Heat’s NBA Cup matchup against the Los Angeles Lakers on F...
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo continues to exert brute force with an incredible highlight during the Miami Heat's NBA Cup matchup against the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night.

Antetokounmpo started the 14th season of his NBA career, his first with the Heat. Following a remarkable tenure with the Milwaukee Bucks, the franchise sent him to Miami as the superstar forward looks to compete for his second championship.

Miami got off to a slow start, losing its first four games. They have since bounced back with back-to-back wins over the Atlanta Hawks and the Pacers, finally gaining traction with their expectations as a squad.

Antetokounmpo balled out in his latest performance in Miami's blowout win over Indiana. One specific highlight among many occurred in the early minutes of the second half. He was inside the paint as he actively secured multiple offensive rebounds , boxing out Indiana players as much as possible before finally getting the shot to go and count the foul he drew.

How Giannis Antetokounmpo, Heat played against Pacers

Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat finally gave home fans their first win, routing the Pacers by a 145-125 score in the NBA Cup group stage.

Six players scored in double-digits for Miami in the win, including Antetokounmpo. He led the squad with a stat line of 31 points, 18 rebounds, 10 assists, and one block. He shot 13-of-19 from the field, including 1-of-2 from beyond the arc, and 4-of-6 from the free-throw line. Bam Adebayo came next with 27 points and nine rebounds, Klay Thompson had 25 points and three assists, while Pelle Larsson put up 18 points and three rebounds. Meanwhile, Davion Mitchell provided 15 points and 11 assists.

Miami improved to a 2-4 record this season, sitting at 10th place in the Eastern Conference standings. They are above the Indiana Pacers and the New York Knicks while trailing the Orlando Magic and the Washington Wizards.

The Heat will look forward to their next matchup, being on the road. They take on the Los Angeles Lakers as tip-off commences on Nov. 2 at 10 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Tyler Reddick on brink of elimination at Martinsville in 2026
articles.summary: Tyler Reddick is on the brink of elimination going into the NASCAR Cup Series race at Martinsville Speedway in 2026.
articles.body:
Tyler Reddick suffered a major setback to his NASCAR Cup Series championship hopes during Sunday's YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway. The 23XI Racing driver started 33rd and ultimately finished 37th after being collected in the massive accident on Lap 132.

Reddick entered the event with momentum after winning the previous race at Phoenix Raceway. That victory had reduced his championship deficit to 56 points behind Kyle Larson with three races remaining.

However, the unpredictable nature of superspeedway racing quickly changed his situation. Reddick was among the drivers involved in the 12-car accident triggered when Ryan Blaney lost momentum in the outside drafting lane.

The damage forced the No. 45 Toyota to the garage and effectively ended Reddick's opportunity to score meaningful points. He ultimately completed 137 laps and finished 37th, collecting just one point. The result left Reddick seventh in the NASCAR Cup Series Chase standings with 2,315 points.

However, his deficit to Larson expanded dramatically from 56 to 126 points. Reddick remains mathematically eligible for the championship, but his chances have been severely diminished. He will need outstanding performances at Martinsville and Homestead-Miami, along with significant problems for Larson, to overcome the deficit.

articles.title: Reagan bounces back from disappointing loss with rout of Roosevelt
articles.summary: Ayden Fernandez and Jericko Espinosa had strong performances on the ground, and the Rattlers put on a clinic on special teams in the win over the Rough Rider...
articles.body:
Sophomore kicker Jacoby Hartofelis lined up to kick a field goal to give Reagan another positive play heading into the locker room, but the ball ended up in senior tight end Russell Reed's hands for something even better.

With four seconds left until halftime, Hartofelis was set for a 28-yard field goal attempt. A bad snap still ended up in holder and senior linebacker Nate Ramos' hands, and he quickly leaped into the air and tossed the ball to Reed for an 11-yard touchdown.

Reagan demonstrated some unexpected creativity on offense to defeat Roosevelt 52-0 Friday night at Comalander Stadium in the penultimate game of the regular season.

"They executed it, but that's not really what we intended," Reagan coach Preston Meyer said of the unexpected score.

Reagan came out firing on all cylinders against Roosevelt, a week after taking a tough 50-7 loss to rival Johnson.

"It shows how much we can face adversity and how much adversity helps a team like us," Reagan senior two-way athlete Ayden Fernandez said of getting back into the win column.

The Rattlers got on the board with a 32-yard rushing touchdown by junior running back Jericko Espinosa in a quick two-minute, five-play drive. Fernandez, Reagan's leading rusher, punched in his first score of the night on an 8-yard rushing touchdown with 7:27 remaining in the second quarter. He recorded his second score of the night with a 31-yard rush to open the scoring in the third quarter.

"We looked very clean," Fernandez said of Reagan's offense. "No mistakes."

Even Reagan's special teams got in on the scoring action before the break. Senior defensive back Landon Herrera returned a punt for a 80-yard touchdown with 3:38 left in the second quarter, minutes before the field goal unit stole their own touchdown.

Senior defensive lineman Colt Galan recovered a loose ball on Roosevelt's 5-yard line in the third quarter after the Rough Riders tried to punt it away. Espinosa quickly ran the ball into the end zone on the ensuing play for a quick score.

"I can't say enough about our kids," Meyer said. "We had a tough one last week, and they came back ready to go to work this week, and we came out and got it done."

Reagan junior kicker Dylan Sage extended the Rattlers' lead with a 37-yard field goal to start the final quarter. Senior running back Alexander Tritch scored Reagan's final touchdown of the night on a 6-yard run with 5:48 to play.

Looking ahead, Reagan is in line for a second-place finish in District 28-6A and has a spot in the playoffs locked up.

"We're going to try and go execute the best we can and get ready to get a good one in the playoffs," Meyer said.

Fernandez hopes the Rattlers will use their final regular season game as a tune up. Reagan takes on Clark next Thursday at Farris Stadium to close out the regular season, while Roosevelt faces Churchill next Friday at Heroes Stadium.

"We've got to play a really clean game," Fernandez said. "Because in playoffs, no mistakes or you lose."

articles.title: Carson Hocevar eliminated from Cup championship contention in 2026
articles.summary: Carson Hocevar has been eliminated from contention in the Chase for the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series championship.
articles.body:
Carson Hocevar overcame significant adversity to finish sixth in Sunday's YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway. The Spire Motorsports driver started 26th and remained competitive despite involvement in the massive accident that sent Joey Logano upside down with five scheduled laps remaining.

Hocevar, who won the spring race at Talladega, was pushing Logano in the outside lane when contact destabilized the No. 22 Ford. The resulting accident collected 15 cars and sent Hocevar's Chevrolet spinning down the frontstretch.

With four flat tires preventing him from driving back to pit road, Hocevar required assistance from a tow truck. His team subsequently repaired the car and returned him to competition without losing a lap.

That recovery proved crucial. Hocevar took advantage of the overtime finish to salvage sixth place, completing all 189 laps despite the earlier damage. The result earned Hocevar 31 points and moved him up one position in the championship standings.

Hocevar now ranks 10th in the NASCAR Cup Series Chase standings with 2,243 points. However, he trails championship leader Kyle Larson by 198 points, mathematically eliminating him from title contention. He will now focus on securing the best possible final championship position over the remaining two races.

articles.title: Ashland's comeback attempt falls short at Canal Winchester in Week 11
articles.summary: The teams combined for 80 points, opposing playmakers combined for 500-plus yards of offense, and it came down to a fourth down stop with 2.2 seconds.
articles.body:
CANAL WINCHESTER — As if Division II, Region 7 needed any further proof it's the strongest in the state, Friday's regional first-round matchup between No. 5 Canal Winchester and No. 12 Ashland was the smoking gun.

After the Arrows snuck into the playoffs as the final qualifier with a win in Week 10 with a .600 record, they were rewarded with a nearly 100-mile trip down to face the Indians. And Ashland made sure that drive was well worth it, pushing Canal Winchester to its limits in a game that featured 80 points between the teams.

In the end, it's the Indians who are moving on to Week 12 thanks to a defensive stop late in the fourth quarter in a 43-37 win.

"That team came in here ready to play and they played their heart out," Canal Winchester coach Corey Coe said. "You gotta give those guys respect because they had nothing to lose coming in here. I know what it's like to have a two-hour bus ride, and for them to come out and play like that, I give those guys a heck of a lot of credit."

Canal Winchester opened the scoring on its first possession, marching down the field with ease and capping off the drive with a 13-yard run from Jamari Snow. The Arrows responded with a Liam Hubacher-to-Killian O'Brien seven-yard connection but missed the extra point to trail by one. Ashland took the lead on a 19-yard field goal from Layton Roop, but that was short-lived as Snow punched in his second to regain the lead with 5:05 in the half.

With a little over a minute to go, before half, Kian McGhee found a wide open Rai'montez Hughley — the Ashland defensive back slipped on the turf — who went for 50 yards setting up Snow's third touchdown of the half, this time from three yards out, for a 21-9 lead at the break.

"We knew coming in that he's good," Ashland coach Scott Valentine said of Snow. "He's a guy we were going to have to tackle and he's just tough to get down. He's a physical guy and he's going to get his yardage, you just gotta try to limit it."

After mustering just nine points in the first half, Ashland exploded for four touchdowns, starting with another Hubacher-to-O'Brien strike from 30 yards out just 31 seconds into the second half. They linked up again from 16 yards out as a response to an 11-yard McGhee keeper on the Indians' first possession. Cody Noble hit a 28-yard field goal for Canal Winchester to push a 31-22 lead that the team would take to the end of the third quarter before then extending that to 37-22 on a Snow one-yard burst up the middle followed by a blocked extra point.

Hubacher called his own number from two yards out less than a minute later. Then, when the Arrows got the ball back again, he found Nevin LaRue in the end zone for the 20-yard score to make it 37-35. And Valentine trusted his quarterback again on the two-point conversion as Hubacher barreled in to tie the game with 3:41 remaining.

Another defensive lapse from the Arrows led to Sir'Anthony Washington wide open for the go-ahead 30-yard score to put the Indians on top 43-37 following another blocked punt.

With under two minutes to play, Killian O'Brien fielded the kickoff and gave the Arrows great field position to which Hubacher marched the team down to the 13. But the drive ended in an incomplete pass in the end zone on fourth down with 2.2 seconds on the clock.

"You gotta make plays one way or the other," Valentine said. "They made a couple plays, and then we had an opportunity to put ourselves in the position — that's all you can ask, right?

Just like a last season's Week 12 clash at St. Francis DeSales, the Arrows had a chance to win it late but came up short.

"It's definitely one of the toughest regions in Ohio," O'Brien said. "And I can't say I hate being part of it because I love the challenge, you get to see some dudes every year. Just two years now we fell by one score ... the opportunity was there; we just couldn't finish."

It was a night where O'Brien became the program's single-season receptions leader (95) after a 12-catch, 187-yard performance with three touchdowns and a week after he nabbed the career receiving yards record (2,746) and extended his career receiving touchdowns mark to 34.

"It means a lot ... I've worked my whole life for this, and it's one of the goals I wanted," O'Brien said. "I'm happy to see myself accomplish it, I just wish we could've got the win tonight."

"He's just an incredible player, an incredible teammate, and an incredible young man," Coe added of O'Brien. "He's really a better person than he is a football player. I'm just proud of his personal development and where he's gone since his freshman year into sophomore year, he just continues to become a better and better young man."

He also had an interception on defense and played a key role on special teams, returning kicks which set up the offense with great field position several times throughout the night.

"This is my best game now," O'Brien said. "There's three phases to the game — special teams, defense, and offense — I gotta do it all when I'm on the field."

It helped having someone on the other side of the field to feed off, too, as Snow finished the night with 35 carries for 314 yards and four touchdowns. The two playmakers combined for 501 yards and seven scores.

"He's a heck of a player and he's their guy," O'Brien said. "They rely on him to do a lot of things, and I feel like I have a lot of weight on my shoulders to do a lot of things. We just had a respectful battle back and forth ... we were hyping each other up."

The loss brings an end to what was a tumultuous season for the Arrows (6-5), who swept their nonleague opposition the first three weeks before dropping the first three games of Ohio Cardinal Conference play. But they closed out winning three of the last four to make the playoffs for the fifth consecutive season.

"Hopefully we learned some lessons," Valentine said. "When you have a young team, they've gotta grow up and they gotta do the work in the off-season. I can go back and look at things from last off-season, and some of the guys didn't think they were going to be playing as much as they ended up playing ... we just gotta get better and work harder in the offseason to get ready for next year."

Canal Winchester (8-3) now shifts its focus to four-seed New Albany (8-2) in a regional quarterfinal. It will be the second time the teams have met this season.

"They're a juggernaut," Coe said. "We were in a slugfest with them last time and ended up beating them 35-28, but I'm sure they probably left that game thinking they didn't play their best. But anytime you get to play New Albany, it's a great opportunity. Our kids are excited for it, and I know they'll be ready for the rematch at their place. This region is incredible and I'm just grateful and proud that we're still playing."

And he's now 6-0 since taking over the program after Week 5 when the Indians fell to 2-3 coming off a narrow loss to Pickerington Central.

"Canal Winchester football is my life, apart from my family," Coe said. "It's a different role I'm still learning — that universal perspective — because I'm a defensive guy and sometimes I gotta be careful about being too defensive-minded on the sideline and be more in-tune with game management. That's not an easy thing when you're still running the show on defense.

"But it's an honor and a privilege, these kids are incredible and I'm proud to be their head coach."

articles.title: Bayern Munich youth player returns after 994 days of injury misery
articles.summary: What a story of determination and resilience.
articles.body:
After nearly three years of waiting, working, and fighting to get back, Bayern Munich U-19 center-back Valentin Beckert has finally made his return.

Beckert suffered through a major ACL injury, followed by a serious hamstring injury, which might have caused him to have doubts that he would ever get back.

Well, he did it—as he returned on Monday to play five minutes against SGV Heilbronn-Freiberg.

It is the kind of moment that puts football into perspective. Behind every comeback is a player who has had to endure countless hours of rehabilitation, frustrating setbacks, and the uncertainty of wondering when the next opportunity will come.

Coming back after such a lengthy absence is an achievement in itself, regardless of what happens next. Getting back onto the pitch after 994 days is a testament to the patience, determination, and resilience required to keep pushing when the finish line feels impossibly far away.

For Beckert, the countdown is over. The focus can finally shift from recovery to football again.

Welcome back, Valentin! Here is hoping the next 994 days are filled with plenty of football, unforgettable moments, and absolutely no more time on the sidelines.

articles.title: Canada’s in-form Leylah Fernandez reaches Pan Pacific Open final in Tokyo
articles.summary: Fernandez fought back from a break down in both sets to reach the Tokyo title clash, her third final of 2026.
articles.body:
Canada’s Leylah Fernandez reached the Tokyo final with a 7-5, 6-3 win over Uzbekistan’s Kamilla Rakhimova on Saturday, continuing her hot streak on the Asian swing.

The World No 23 won her first title of the season in Singapore last month and followed that up by reaching the final of last week’s Ningbo Open in China, where she lost to World No 1 Elena Rybakina .

Fernandez will face either Russia’s Diana Shnaider or Slovakia’s Mia Pohankova in the final of the WTA 500 Pan Pacific Open on Sunday, as she aims for her seventh WTA Tour title.

Fernandez reached the semifinals when Rybakina withdrew from their match with a neck injury, a day after securing the year-end world No1 ranking.

Rakhimova, ranked 66th, was eliminated in qualifying in Tokyo but entered the main draw as a lucky loser and made it all the way to the semifinals.

She was attempting to reach her first final on the WTA Tour, but ran into a player in form in Fernandez, who hit nine aces.

The Canadian went a break down early in the first set but soon recovered with a break of her own, before tipping the balance her way.

Rakhimova also went a break up early in the second set, but Fernandez clawed her way back and took the match in just less than two hours.

articles.title: Hakimi’s hat-trick guides PSG to stunning 5-1 win at Le Havre in Ligue 1
articles.summary: European champions PSG registered their sixth league victory and sit two points clear at top of the Ligue 1 standings.
articles.body:
Flying ‌fullback Achraf Hakimi grabbed a hat-trick as Paris Saint-Germain went on a rampage to thrash ⁠bottom-placed Le Havre 5-1 and extend their Ligue 1 lead on Friday.

The European champions , who have several regulars out injured, could afford to leave ⁠more of their key players on the bench and still come away with an impressive victory as they moved to 20 points from their opening nine league fixtures.

They ⁠are two points ahead of Lille and four above third-placed Rennes, who have 16 points.

Lille moved above Rennes into second, thanks to a late goal from veteran Olivier Giroud, who came off the bench to score an 86th-minute winner for a 1-0 derby ‌victory at home over RC Lens.

Rennes were handed a 5-2 drubbing at Nice, who continued their improving form with a fourth win in five outings.

Elye Wahi netted a hat-trick for Nice, who moved up to seventh after narrowly avoiding relegation last season.

On top of his three goals at Stade Oceane, Hakimi had two assists for the goals scored by Mika Godts and Senny Mayulu after Josh Maja had given the ⁠hosts the lead.

It was PSG’s ninth consecutive victory in all ⁠competitions.

Le Havre suffered a fifth consecutive defeat and sit bottom with two points, but they briefly dared to believe as Maja handed them an early lead.

Hakimi set up Godts for the equaliser before putting his side ⁠ahead in the 28th minute with a shot in at the near post.

The Morocco international then netted from a free kick ⁠into the bottom corner in the 55th minute before ⁠being at the centre of a counterattack that saw Mayulu make it 4-1 in the 62nd minute.

Hakimi completed his hat-trick with a deflected effort in the 69th minute.

“I am happy because some players had very ‌little playing time. If we want to win trophies, we need everyone,” said PSG coach Luis Enrique.

articles.title: Una mente a otra velocidad: el TDAH en el deporte de élite
articles.standfirst: Este trastorno de origen neurobiológico cursa con hiperactividad, impulsividad y déficit de atención. Giménez, Amaia Alday o Jero García, para los que el deporte ha sido clave, ejemplos
articles.summary: Este trastorno de origen neurobiológico cursa con hiperactividad, impulsividad y déficit de atención. Giménez, Amaia Alday o Jero García, para los que el deporte ha sido clave, ejemplos
articles.body: Mi infancia fue complicada. Me sentía diferente, no encajaba. Veía que el resto podía llevar a cabo las tareas diarias de una forma ordenada y normal y yo dejaba los trabajos para el final. No atendía, a veces incluso me costaba mantenerme concentrada en cosas que realmente me gustaban. En clase, al estar quieta notaba como si tuviese corriente por dentro del cuerpo, necesitaba moverme porque si no, me empezaba a agobiar, me angustiaba. Al final era frustrante”. Amaia Alday (Dima, 2000), campeona en tres ocasiones del Cuatro y Medio de pelota vasca, creció sin entender qué le ocurría o por qué muchos adultos de su entorno le decían que era vaga e inquieta y ella no lo podía evitar. Algo similar le ocurrió a José María Giménez (Toledo -Uruguay-, 1985), actual jugador del Deportivo y uno de los grandes capitanes del Atlético de Madrid en la ‘era Simeone’. “Fui un niño súper inquieto, con muchísima energía. Todo el tiempo quería jugar, correr... También era el típico niño que se portaba mal. Estaba todo el tiempo queriendo llamar la atención. En clase me aburría, molestaba a los compañeros. Siempre me fue bien en los estudios, pero me condenaba muchísimo el tema de la conducta”, asegura a MARCA. Ambos deportistas tienen TDAH (Trastorno por Déficit de Atención e Hiperactividad), un trastorno de origen neurobiológico en el que existe un funcionamiento diferente de la parte prefrontal del cerebro, cuyas manifestaciones pueden cursar con déficit de atención, hiperactividad e impulsividad, en distintos grados y frecuencias. “Se trata de una neurodiversidad biológica, una disfunción neurológica que afecta a aquellas funciones ejecutivas o situaciones diarias que requieren un funcionamiento adecuado”, explica a MARCA Maite Urkizu, psicopedagoga, especialista en conducta y en TDAH y coordinadora de la asociación ADAHIGI de Gipuzkoa. “Hablamos, por tanto, de poder mantener la atención, la planificación, la gestión emocional, el recuerdo de actos pasados, el ser capaz de gestionar las repercusiones y la toma de decisiones en base a esas consecuencias... Es mucho más que decir que una persona no presta atención, se mueve o es impulsivo”. En los últimos años el TDAH, como otras neurodivergencias, se ha visto rodeado de falsas creencias y mitos que en ocasiones dificultan identificar un trastorno que afecta a más de 4,2 millones de personas en España. “El diagnóstico es sanitario y debe ser multidisciplinar”, apunta Urkizu. “Se realizan pruebas psicométricas que suman muchísima información al diagnóstico sanitario posterior. Pero también se valoran las dificultades que se perciben en varios ambientes: colegio, amigos, casa... Con cuestionarios y una visión evolutiva de cómo ha sido el proceso de ese niño y adolescente, el sanitario puede dictaminar el TDAH”. La detección temprana de este trastorno, del que ya había bibliografía médica documentada en siglos pasados, es crucial, pero en ocasiones la falta de información resulta un obstáculo para ello. “Siempre me decían que era vaga, movida, pero nadie me habló del TDAH”, recuerda a MARCA Amaia Alday. “En casa también tuve muchos conflictos con mis padres. No nos entendíamos. Yo jugué al fútbol desde los 9 hasta los 20 años, pero era una persona bastante impulsiva, que no sabía controlar todo lo que sentía. En los entrenamientos y en los partidos a veces tenía problemas. Cuando el entrenador explicaba algún ejercicio, yo nunca me enteraba de lo que había que hacer. Y en mitad de un partido, entre el ruido de la grada y del campo, mi técnico me intentaba hablar, pero yo tenía demasiados estímulos y no podía prestar atención a uno solo. Además, tenía altibajos en el juego, lo hacía muy bien los primeros 20-30 minutos de los 50 que estaba en el campo porque me desconcentraba”. Eso llevó a Amaia a dejar el fútbol y empezar a jugar a pelota vasca. “En el frontón, tenía diversas actitudes que no sabía gestionar, como pegar golpes a la pared, lanzar la pelota... Así, a los 20 años pedí asesoramiento a un psicólogo y ahí me diagnosticaron TDAH”. Según estudios realizados, y pese a que en ocasiones existe infradiagnóstico, la prevalencia de este trastorno entre los deportistas profesionales de élite es del 7%-8%, mientras que en la población adulta general apenas alcanza el 5%, estadísticas que puede respaldar la ciencia. “Un cerebro TDAH funciona de manera diferente porque hay dos neurotransmisores que no tienen la misma intensidad de acción: la dopamina y la noradrenalina”, explica Maite Urkizu. “La parte prefrontal del cerebro se activa porque esa sustancia está en el nivel óptimo y arranca. ¿Qué hace el deporte? Generar estos dos neurotransmisores. Por lo tanto, el deportista va a tener ese plus porque el deporte se lo está dando de forma natural. Además, por el factor neurotrópico derivado del cerebro, la persona que hace deporte estará en una condición mayor de concentración, regulación emocional y control de la impulsividad”. Dicha impulsividad es otro de los rasgos del TDAH y el deporte ayuda a canalizarlo. “De niño yo sentía que iba a una velocidad completamente distinta a los demás”, recuerda Jero García, exboxeador, entrenador y presidente de la Fundación de Ayuda a la Integración a través del Deporte que lleva su nombre. “Y eso, en el contexto del Carabanchel de los años 80, me llevó a abrazar la violencia como forma de reafirmarme. Culturalmente era lo que vivía y me di cuenta de que me regulaba emocionalmente. Con 8 años me expulsaron del colegio por primera vez porque le hice una zancadilla a la profesora. Tenía una impulsividad que no era normal. Si la liaba, me sentía bien y empecé a delinquir, con pequeños hurtos... hasta que tuve un susto mayor y dije que no podía seguir así”. Tras darse cuenta de que en el fútbol, aun jugando ya en Preferente con 18 años, no podía seguir (“me tiraba expulsado un partido sí, uno no”), Jero se abrazó al ‘noble arte’. “Encontré la paz entre los golpes”, explica el exboxeador. “Regular la ira y canalizar la agresividad me hacían encontrar la estabilidad emocional que hacía 20 años que no tenía. El boxeo me aportó muchísimos valores: disciplina, constancia, motivación, solidaridad, pertenencia al grupo... y eso lo pude extrapolar a mi vida”. Tanto en el caso de Amaia Alday como en el de Jero García y José María Giménez el diagnóstico llegó en la etapa adulta, a veces por la detección de este trastorno a alguno de los vástagos. “A mi hijo mediano, Luciano, le empezaron a etiquetar de insoportable, de peleón...”, explica el jugador del Depor. “Como padre me empecé a preocupar por la situación. Quise buscar respuestas a su forma de ser. Muchas veces no lo entendíamos, tenía comportamientos que me recordaban a mí cuando era pequeño. Fuimos a un centro muy bueno en Madrid, especializado en niños con trastornos, y a partir de ahí empezamos con los estudios”. Llegaron entonces las pruebas, las preguntas, los análisis, los cuestionarios... “Le dieron el diagnóstico de TDAH a mi hijo y después el especialista me miró y me dijo ‘papi, esto es hereditario’. En ese momento, no sé por qué, me puse a llorar, porque yo me decía: ‘Tanto tiempo viviendo con él y no lo sabía entender, no lo podía entender’. A partir de ahí fue un antes y un después en nuestras vidas”. Recibir el diagnóstico del TDAH supone hallar la pieza del puzzle que permite comprender y contextualizar que aquellas emociones, patrones y actitudes incomprendidos y criticados en muchas ocasiones desde la infancia no eran fallas sino características de una mente neurodivergente que interpreta la vida de otra manera. “Me pusieron medicación y ya con el diagnóstico empecé a entenderme y a aceptarme a mí mismo”, admite Giménez. “Porque antes me frustraba mucho el hecho de que me iba a dormir y era el momento en el que todo me venía a la cabeza. Ahora descanso muchísimo mejor y me tomo el día con más calma. Fue un paso muy importante en mi vida para empezar a ser yo desde lo que tengo”. Aunque el TDAH puede condicionar algunos aspectos de la vida, permite tener desempeños extraordinarios en otras facetas y el deporte es una de ellas. “Tenemos dos capacidades maravillosas que normalmente están siempre a favor del deportista con TDAH si tiene aptitudes para esa disciplina”, analiza Urkizu. “Uno es el hiper foco: ante el reto, ante la motivación del enganche, ante lo que supone el subidón de la competición, los deportistas con TDAH van a estar al 100% para llevar a cabo ese deporte. Y el otro es la regulación: como estoy a nivel neurológico y a nivel neurotransmisor correctamente, voy a poder regular muchísimo más. Eso les facilita que en los momentos en los que deben estar al límite, den el máximo”. Así lo corroboran los deportistas, que sienten que el deporte fue un sostén que les ayudó física y anímicamente de niños y que terminó siendo su profesión. “Cuando yo corría por todos lados en el campo, era mejor que cuando corría en el salón de casa. Al final me sentía en libertad y eso fue gracias al fútbol”, recuerda Giménez. Los hándicaps de estos perfiles, sin embargo, pueden ser la falta de constancia y la gestión de la frustración. “Yo he visto a un atleta con TDAH estar a tope en una competición y batir su propio récord y al siguiente fin de semana ni siquiera pasar las eliminatorias en otro evento”, recuerda Maite. Por eso es esencial la labor de los psicólogos deportivos expertos en neurodivergencias, que puedan trabajar con deportistas en edades tempranas para enseñarles a gestionar esa frustración y a tener la constancia que necesitan para, si tienen las aptitudes, llegar y brillar en la élite. Además, es clave trabajar la autoestima y la aceptación de un trastorno que sigue perseguido por el estigma. “De alguna manera vas cerrando heridas, pensamientos que te perturbaban: por qué hice o pasó esto”, admite Giménez. “Muchas veces he tomado una decisión y he hecho o dicho algo que en realidad no quería hacer ni decir y en el momento me doy cuenta y me arrepiento, pero el daño ya está hecho. Hoy entiendes que muchos de esos comportamientos y actitudes fueron parte de esto”. Por eso, la visibilización y pedagogía sobre esta neurodivergencia resultan imprescindibles, por lo que la Federación Española de Asociaciones de TDAH ha realizado una campaña de sensibilización en octubre, dentro del Mes europeo de concienciación sobre este trastorno, para acompañar, derribar mitos y reivindicar derechos: “El estigma no está en las personas que tenemos TDAH sino en que la sociedad sigue viéndonos mal”, señala Urkizu. “De hecho muchas veces el diagnóstico les libera de pensar que ‘tengo un hijo malo’, ‘soy mala persona’, ‘yo no lo hacía adrede’, ‘no era el vago’, ‘no era el maleducado’, sino que hay una explicación neurológica para entender cómo funcionaba”. Con los ajustes, adaptaciones y estrategias adecuadas, las personas con TDAH alcanzan todas las metas que se proponen... aunque sea de una forma diferente. “Yo estoy orgulloso de ser TDAH y soy lo que soy también gracias a ello”, admite Jero García. “Como dice el gran Toni Nadal, todo se entrena... Hasta el TDAH”.

articles.standfirst: Joanna Wietrzyk es la mejor en la cita de Hamburgo que marca el inicio de la nueva temporada
articles.summary: Joanna Wietrzyk es la mejor en la cita de Hamburgo que marca el inicio de la nueva temporada
articles.body: Joanna Wietrzyk, la deportista que acabó cubierta de heces una prueba de hyrox en Pekín, se alzó con la victoria en la primera prueba de la temporada que acaba de arrancar en Hamburgo. La australiana, plusmarquista mundial, marcó el mejor tiempo tras completar todas las pruebas en 56:10. Aventajó en 14 segundos a Laura Weeks y en 1:45 a Vivian Tafuto. Wietrzyk, antes de la competición, había vuelto a pedir disculpas por lo sucedido en Pekín y a reiterar que debería de haberse salido de la pista. "Durante las últimas seis u ocho semanas he tenido tiempo para reflexionar sobre todo lo sucedido en Pekín y, en primer lugar, quiero decir que lo siento muchísimo por todos los que se vieron afectados, ya fueran espectadores o participantes en la pista, por mi decisión de seguir compitiendo”, comentó en su cuenta de Instagram. “Tras este tiempo de reflexión, he aprendido mucho de la situación y lo lamento profundamente. Ha sido una situación muy difícil de sobrellevar para mí y también muy difícil de afrontar, así que todo el apoyo, ya sea personal o a través de mi equipo, ha sido sinceramente increíble y significa mucho más de lo que puedo expresar ahora mismo. Estoy muy emocionada de volver a hacer lo que me apasiona”, añadió. Estas palabras las repitió luego en una entrevista concedida a la BBC en la que recordó lo que pasó en la cita de Pekín: "No fue hasta casi la mitad de la carrera cuando todo sucedió... En ese momento, justo ahí, como persona muy competitiva. y como atleta de élite que soy, mi único objetivo era competir. Obviamente puse en riesgo a otras personas", admitió. Wietrzyk habló también de lo mal que lo pasó ella y su familia por los comentarios que le llegaron a través de la redes sociales: "Sí, tomé la decisión equivocada, pero no creo que mereciera recibir tantas críticas ni estar sometida a un escrutinio tan intenso en internet... Al fin y al cabo, solo soy un ser humano".

articles.title: Beat Luke Littler: Fallon Sherrock delighted to 'overcome the hate' and beat Littler in one-off leg to claim £501k prize
articles.summary: Fallon Sherrock defeated 'The Nuke' in the 'Beat Luke Littler' darts event on Netflix but her participation attracted criticism from some quarters; watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
The 32-year-old was crowned champion of Netflix's 'Beat Luke Littler' on Friday night after she overcame the double world champion in a one-off leg of 501 to claim a mammoth £501,000 prize.

Only Littler himself has taken more from a single prize pot, the £1million he collected for his second World Championship in January.

This was not Sherrock's first foray into the limelight, as she created history by becoming the first woman to win at the World Championship when she made the third round seven years ago and she went on to break several other barriers in the game.

But her inclusion in the line-up for the TV show attracted criticism given her stature in the game, even if she met the criteria for applicants because she does not hold a PDC Tour Card.

"I mean it's been tough," she said. "Because obviously I do see the backlash and I do see all the negative comments.

"But at the end of the day, I fit the criteria for this. I've never had a tour card, and I wouldn't class myself as a pro really, because all I do is just play darts for the enjoyment of it.

"I think people forget where I started off as well. When I won at the Worlds, I was still just doing WDF (World Darts Federation).

"I'm just so happy to overcome all the hate and win."

Sherrock, who was the 15th competitor to take on Littler, was joined in the line-up by WDF number one Mitchell Lawrie, Mark Pooke, who played Phil Taylor in a professional event almost 20 years ago, and prodigious teenager Jayden Walker, who has taken a leg off Littler at an exhibition event.

There were also everyday players such as a bin man, an Australian jockey and a Nando's manager.

PDC chief Barry Hearn, who was involved in the audition process, defended the line-up.

Asked whether Sherrock's inclusion was unfair, he was unequivocal.

"No, not at all," said Hearn. "She's not a PDC Tour Card holder. She's entitled to enter. Why should she be denied?

"She's a well-known player and she's a very good player. But Mitchell Lawrie is a very well-known player and an excellent player.

"Do you want just a series of 20 matches where someone can't even throw a dart? No, of course we want excellence competing against excellence, and that's what it was all about."

articles.title: Liverpool vs Arsenal: Premier League – Predictions, news, teams, lineups
articles.summary: Arsenal, second in the table, travel to Anfield looking to bounce back from their shock League Cup fourth-round exit.
articles.body:
Who : Liverpool vs Arsenal What : English Premier League, match day 9 When : Sunday, November 1, 16:30 GMT Where : Anfield, Liverpool, United Kingdom How to follow : Al Jazeera will provide build-up and live updates from 13:30 GMT.

Humiliated by one of the most chastening defeats in their club’s glittering history, Arsenal have a chance to erase the embarrassment of their League Cup loss at Fleetwood Town when they face Premier League title rivals Liverpool on Sunday.

Mikel Arteta’s side were left shell-shocked by their penalty shootout exit against fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood following a dismal display in Tuesday’s 1-1 draw.

The Premier League champions were so far below their best that it was hard to believe this was the same team that stormed to the title last term and looked hungry to retain the crown in the opening weeks of this season.

A victory at Anfield would restore Arsenal’s belief, but in-form Liverpool will be no pushovers, especially on their home turf.

Heading into the match on a five-game winning streak, Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool are in a confident mood, and the Reds can move within three points of the Gunners if they win this weekend’s marquee match-up.

Here’s everything you need to know about Liverpool vs Arsenal:

How have Premier League holders Arsenal fared this season?

Arsenal are second in the Premier League standings on 21 points after eight games, sitting behind leaders Manchester City on goal difference. The Gunners have won seven league games and lost just once – a 3-0 defeat at Brighton last month.

In the Champions League, they are seventh in the league standings with two wins and a draw.

However, they were knocked out of the League Cup in the fourth round after losing 5-3 on penalties to fourth-tier Fleetwood.

Liverpool are fourth in the league standings on 15 points, six points off the top of the table. The Reds have won four games, drawn three and lost once.

In the Champions League, they are third with three wins in three, and have qualified for the League Cup quarterfinals after beating Chelsea 6-5 on penalties midweek.

Opta’s supercomputer has given Arsenal a 41.8 percent probability of winning this game at Anfield.

Liverpool have a 32.7 percent chance, while the odds of a draw stand at 25.5 percent.

(Last five games in all competitions; latest match first)

Andoni Iraola (Liverpool): “It’s still October; take one game at a time, and I always say the first reference is normally when we have played ‌against each other once, halfway through the season, and then you can start looking at the standings.

“Now we are in a position where we need to improve, keep getting better. Can fans dream? It’s good if they have expectations and think we can win. But if you ask me, it is still early.”

Mikel Arteta (Arsenal): “We expect a big game on Sunday; we’re looking forward to it for sure. It’s been 14 years since we last won there, so it’s time to do it.”

Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool): “It’s a night like this [against Chelsea] and the other night [Villarreal] – the fans definitely like what they’re seeing and, of course, you feel that energy and it’s great.

“I’ve been feeling that energy for quite a while and when you then miss it a little bit, then to get it back is obviously very good. Results help, massively. We understand it as well.”

Martin Odegaard (Arsenal): “Obviously, the way we played (against Fleetwood) was not on the level. We need to do much, much better than we did.

“We can’t feel sorry for ourselves. We need to move on; we have a big game at the weekend, so bouncing back is all we can do now.”

Liverpool have a long list of injured players: Hugo Ekitike (Achilles tendon), Jeremie Frimpong (hamstring), Conor Bradley (knee) and Giovanni Leoni (cruciate ligament).

Dominik Szoboszlai could feature after recovering from a hamstring injury.

Alisson; Ronald Araujo, Jeremy Jacquet, Virgil van Dijk, Milos Kerkez; Ryan Gravenberch, Alexis Mac Allister; Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo; Alexander Isak

Arsenal also have several players sidelined with injuries: Bukayo Saka (muscle), William Saliba (back), Christos Tzolis (hamstring) and Toni Madueke (ankle).

Declan Rice and Riccardo Calafiori have resumed training after missing the Fleetwood match.

articles.title: Se lleva medio millón de euros tras ganar a Luke Littler en una partida de dardos
articles.standfirst: Fallon Sherrock derrotó al campeón del mundo en el evento organizado por Netflix
articles.summary: Fallon Sherrock derrotó al campeón del mundo en el evento organizado por Netflix
articles.body: Luke Littler, el 'Niño Maravilla' de los dardos, aceptó el reto de Netflix. La plataforma audiovisual puso en marcha un evento televisivo en el que, tras varias eliminatorias regionales, 20 participantes se enfrentaría al campeón del mundo en una sola ronda de 501. Si alguno le ganaba se llevaría 501.000 libras esterlinas (586.042 euros). Fallon Sherrock lo logró. "Es un momento increíble y lo recordaré para siempre. Si me dan una oportunidad, la aprovecho siempre. Estoy muy orgullosa de mí misma, siempre doy la talla", comentó Sherrock tras ganar la partida. Ella no es una desconocida en el mundo de los dardos. Fue la primera mujer en vencer a un jugador masculino en el Mundial de la PDC (Corporación Profesional de Dardos) para meterse en los dieciseisavos de final en diciembre de 2019. Venció a Ted Evetts y Mensur Suljovic antes de perder contra Chris Dobey. A sus 32 años ha ganado 21 veces en la competición femenina de la PDC. Sherrock cerró sus tiradas, primero con un 180 (tres dardos en el triple 20). Se quedó a 43 puntos del 501. En su siguiente lanzamiento mandó un dardo al 3. Buscó el doble 20. Falló en el primer intento. En el segundo lo clavó. "Ella estuvo brillante, eso es lo que tenía que hacer una persona: ganar la diana y salir en 15 [dardos] y eso es lo que hizo, de clase mundial", comentó Littler. Hubo 25.000 aspirantes que se presentaron al concurso. En la primera fase, los jugadores debían bajar de 501 puntos en 24 dardos o menos. Quienes lo consiguieron pasaron un entrevista con el 16 veces campeón del mundo Phil Taylor, el presidente de la PDC, Barry Hearn, y la comentarista televisiva de dardos Laura Turner. Dieciséis jugadores fueron seleccionados directamente, mientras que ocho jugadores con más experiencia fueron emparejados, y los espectadores de Netflix votaron para decidir qué cuatro debería poder competir. Sherrock se midó al alemán Jarod Becker y obtuvo el 75% de los votos. Algunas voces criticaron su presencia en este evento amateur por considerar que aunque no es profesional, su nivel estaba muy por encima de la esencia de este torneo. Antes que Fallon Sherrock, Pearse Mackle, un estudiante universitario de 21 años que compite en el Circuito de Desarrollo de la PDC, tuvo en su mano derrotar a Littler. Dispuso de un lanzamiento para ganar la partida, pero no pudo acertar en la diana.

articles.title: Linda Cohn says ESPN cut her salary by 80 percent: ‘Loyalty doesn’t pay’
articles.summary: Linda Cohn has talked a lot about “total freedom” since retiring from ESPN this June and starting her eponymous podcast shortly thereafter. The all-time reco...
articles.body:
Linda Cohn has talked a lot about " total freedom " since retiring from ESPN this June and starting her eponymous podcast shortly thereafter. The all-time record-holding SportsCenter host is certainly speaking freely about what really happened during her 34 years at ESPN, at least from her perspective.

This week, Cohn appeared on The Sage Steele Show for a lengthy conversation, largely about their past lives as colleagues at ESPN. (Sage Steele d eparted ESPN after settling a free-speech lawsuit in August 2023, having spent 16 years at the company.)

An hour in, Steele stated that the majority of her years were "awesome" at ESPN, while the remaining 10 percent was "devastating," with which Cohn agreed. Cohn disclosed memories of "sobbing in the ladies' room multiple times" from "dealing with people who made me feel like crap on the air."

"I did not understand, with the National Hockey League, I was one of few people that kept that damn sport alive on SportsCenter , and then I was cast aside," Cohn said, adding, "That hurt me. That really hurt me. They put me basically—and thank God I had Barry [Melrose] most of the time to host 'In The Crease,' when I should have been out there on the ice with those players, covering Stanley Cup Finals or being rink side. But after the first year and a half, I was cast aside, and suddenly, they didn't use me at all. And they just put me in that SportsCenter box."

Cohn clarified she wasn't complaining about hosting SportsCenter , and she said she "never got an answer" as to why ESPN didn't use her more directly for NHL-central coverage.

"The last year, technically, I was at ESPN, they cut my salary 80 percent after they closed the L.A. studio," Cohn said.

Cohn additionally noted that her colleagues working on the Los Angeles-based SportsCenter , which shuttered in May 2025 , received six weeks' notice to either relocate to the main Bristol campus or essentially become unemployed.

"At that point, my deal was up, and I was like, 'I'm not gonna let them rush me into a decision,'" Cohn said. "And I didn't end my tenure that way. So I accepted their 80 percent pay cut."

Cohn said she spoke to ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro, and while she thought "the call went well," she felt ESPN's actions showed otherwise.

"I actually signed a deal that [said], OK, Linda, you can do 15 events or appearances for us, but we're cutting your salary 80 percent," Cohn said. "Sage, loyalty doesn't pay because I'll tell you something. What people think I made, or if you google me and what I made, that's all incorrect. Trust me on that."

Ultimately, Cohn said, she did five events for ESPN and felt "out of sight, out of mind" until the contract expired in June. Cohn told Steele she still felt like ESPN pushed her out, saying, "They had no place for a Linda Cohn in their mind." Still, Cohn said, "it all worked out."

Cohn launched The Linda Cohn Show independently in July, and she officially partnered with Bleav in late September.

"For the first time, I'm not in a box," Cohn said of her podcast. "For the first time, I don't have a muzzle around my mouth. A gag! I was able to talk about how I was feeling about certain things. Now, it's a sports show. But it's a sports topical show. It's stuff off the court, off the field."

articles.title: Packers’ Josh Jacobs Faces New Allegations Before Vikings Rematch
articles.summary: At least three more women have reported accusations of abuse against Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The post Packers’ Josh Jacobs Faces New Alle...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings have a rematch of their Week 1 showdown with the NFC North Division rival Green Bay Packers two weeks from now, but the status of Josh Jacobs could be in question after new allegations surfaced against the Packers running back.

NBC 26 in Northeast Wisconsin reported on Friday, October 30 that multiple other females came forward and accused Jacobs of abuse following his arrest on domestic charges in May of this year.

"Newly released records show additional women contacted the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department to report alleged physical incidents involving Packers running back Josh Jacobs," NBC 26 reported. "These allegations are detailed in a heavily-redacted Hobart-Lawrence Police Department case file released to NBC 26 late Friday, which also provides new details in the incident that led to Jacobs' arrest in May."

NFL Has Not Concluded Investigation Into Josh Jacobs' Domestic Incident in May

Jacobs pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor counts, one of battery and the other of criminal damage to property, in early September. Those pleas came as a result of the May 2026 incident.

The NFL kept Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List for the first six weeks of the season, which is the equivalent to paid leave, granting him eligibility to play in Week 7 against the Detroit Lions .

Jacobs has appeared in the team's last two contests, though the league has not closed its investigation into the running back, even despite the conclusion of the legal matters that included court punishments that did not involve any jail time for the Packers running back.

The NFL continues to seek a video of the incident in May, which it the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department could release via public records requests depending on the outcome of lawsuits filed by both Jacobs and the victim to keep said evidence permanently sealed.

Josh Jacobs Subject of Several Separate Allegations of Abuse by Alleged Female Victims

Following the news of Jacobs' domestic incident in May, a second purported victim came forward to police in June with accusations that the Packers running back had been physically abusive toward her in a separate incident.

"Per the records, the woman, who was not identified, contacted investigators in June after learning about the May investigation, telling police the allegations sounded similar to her prior experience with Jacobs [in January of 2022]," NBC 26 reported further. "She said the incident had never been reported to law enforcement. She said she contacted police when she believed her alleged experience with Jacobs could be relevant to the case and also because she wanted people to believe the woman involved in the May 2026 incident that led to Jacobs' arrest."

This second woman's accounting events alleged that Jacobs "slapped her across the face, grabbed her by the hair, threw her onto a bed, pinned her down, threw her onto the floor, spit on her and grabbed her by the throat. She also said Jacobs took her phone as she attempted to leave his home."

Josh Jacobs' Alleged Actions Against Multiple Women Described in Detail

Two other women came forward with allegations toward Jacobs as well. One alleged that in April of 2021 "Jacobs grabbed her by the arms, pushed her against a wall near a window and threw her belongings outside the home. She said she suffered bruising to her arms and pain and swelling in her rib area."

NBC 26 reported that the woman had no visible signs of injury upon her report, according to the relevant police department, so authorities never filed charges.

A third woman reported via a phone call to the Hobart/Lawerence Police Department that in May of 2022 "Jacobs placed his hands on her head and neck, dragged her, scratched her chest, and took possession of her cell phone after it fell to the floor."

The alleged victim added that "she suffered bruising to her arm and scratches to her chest which she said remained visible for about a month, according to the records. The woman told Hobart/Lawrence Police she did not report the incident to police or seek medical treatment at the time. She said Jacobs told her she could be deported, and because of that she did not believe she could report the incident to law enforcement."

articles.title: Mansoor Delane shares lessons learned from covering Jaxon Smith-Njigba
articles.summary: During his press conference, Kansas City Chiefs DB Mansoor Delane discussed lessons from covering Seattle Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba | @EdEastonJr
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs defensive back Mansoor Delane recently spoke with reporters. He shared lessons learned from a tough Week 7 matchup against Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

"Really just prepares me. I think there's great receivers on every team; you've just got to bring it, and you've got to prepare, and they're going to win some, you're going to win some," said Delane. "So just really having that short-term mentality, whether it's good or bad, and just having an expert mentality."

The reigning NFL offensive player of the year got the better of the impressive Chiefs rookie. Delane is using the experience as additional motivation as he looks to match up against the league's best wide receivers moving forward.

"Yeah, for sure. I think some people may get discouraged from passes caught on them. But I told Coach (Steve) Spags (Spagnuolo), 'Man, put me in those tough situations.' I'm not asking for a cloud. I'm not asking for cover two. Go back out there and play man, and that's what we did," said Delane. "Like, a lot of teams are kind of scared to do that. But I feel like we didn't shy away from it. So, we learned from it, but at the same time, it's going to be times in my career that I'm going to better handle that stick, and I'm definitely going to learn from that."

Delane has recorded 17 total tackles (10 solo, 7 assisted), 1 interception, and 5 passes defended over 5 games in his rookie season.

No. 12 Ole Miss (5-2, 3-2 SEC) hosts Auburn (4-3, 2-3) on Oct. 31 (11:45 a.m., SEC Network).

Chambliss had worked himself up to being the frontrunner early in the season, but fell after a loss to Florida. He was +650 entering Week 8 at Texas but was 25-for-52 with two touchdowns and three interceptions in a loss to the Longhorns on Oct. 24.

Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss quarterback, Heisman candidate for Pete Golding in 2026

Chambliss has fallen out of the leading pack of Heisman Trophy favorites, but he remains in contention for college football's highest award.

Through seven games in 2026, Chambliss is completing 63.7% of his passes. He has 1,926 passing yards, 16 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has 41 rushes for 134 yards and six touchdowns.

Ole Miss coach Pete Golding has alluded to Chambliss increasing his rushing attempts with running back Kewan Lacy sidelined with a shoulder injury.

Chambliss finished eighth in the 2025 Heisman Trophy voting.
