articles.title: Indiana football playoffs: 6-foot-4 safety Jake Jaeger is big obstacle as Crown Point stops Merrillville
articles.summary: Crown Point junior free safety Jake Jaeger snagged one interception and nearly made two more against Merrillville on Friday night. But the 6-foot-4, 195-poun...
articles.body:
Crown Point junior free safety Jake Jaeger snagged one interception and nearly made two more against Merrillville on Friday night.

But the 6-foot-4, 195-pound Jaeger wasn't complaining after the Class 6A sectional semifinal between Duneland Athletic Conference rivals.

"We just rallied together," Jaeger said. "No matter what happens, the score's always 0-0 in our eyes. We just played together, and we didn't break. We came close, but we didn't break."

Indeed, Crown Point held off host Merrillville 43-33 in a dazzling and dizzying matchup pitting the area's top two teams and two of the state's best.

The Bulldogs (10-0), who were ranked No. 4 in the final Class 6A state coaches poll, led 29-0 and nearly triggered a running clock before the Pirates (8-2) drew as close as 29-27.

Jaeger's third interception of the season is tied for the team lead after senior cornerback Jaden Saddler also made one in the waning minutes against the Pirates. Jaeger had a pick-six during the Bulldogs' regular-season finale against Michigan City.

"Jake Jaeger has done a great job," Crown Point coach Craig Buzea said. "It's his first year playing free safety, and he's done an outstanding job. I ask coach (John) Snyder (the team's defensive coordinator) who he wants to be captain every week because we pick game captains, and Jake's always in that conversation. He's done a great job leading. He's just a fantastic, fantastic kid and a dual-sport athlete, and he really did a good job directing our secondary.

"He's just an athlete, and he's going to get better. I think he'll find himself, if he wants to go play at the next level, because he's only a junior, he'll be able to do that just with this length and size, and he's worked hard. He's worked his butt off to get to where he's at."

Jaeger, who has also played basketball for Crown Point, agreed he was dedicated to making strides with both his skills and his strength. Last season, he played primarily on the junior varsity team and had 14 tackles in a largely mop-up role behind three-year starter Dominic Fantin.

"I used to be pretty nervous before games," Jaeger said. "I've been calming my nerves down and just playing football."

Jaeger, who has 16 tackles this season, has been doing it at a high level.

"Jake's really good," Crown Point sophomore quarterback/linebacker AJ Summers said. "He covers that field really well. He had to fill big shoes with Dom Fantin from last year, and he definitely filled them. He's doing a great job back there."

Jaeger even drew praise from Merrillville senior quarterback Michael Hill Jr. , who nearly engineered a stunning comeback by completing 31 of 54 pass attempts for 415 yards and five TDs.

"He's just back there," Hill said. "He's tall, he's long, and it's just hard to really get the deep balls over him."

As for Summers, he generally ran over and through defenders. He rushed for 222 yards and five TDs on 28 carries.

Buzea enthusiastically extolled Summers' virtues.

"I think we all witnessed the best player in high school football," Buzea said. "No. 4 is the best player in Indiana. I don't care if he's a sophomore, a junior, a senior. What he does at a 6A level, nobody does. Against a team like that?

"Now, did he have help? Yes, our offensive line was tremendous. But AJ Summers is the best player in Indiana. That's what I witnessed. Incredible. Incredible. He's on the field every play for defense. I haven't coached many kids like him, and he's 16 years old. I know it, I get it — people know he's going to run the ball. But you have to stop him."

Behind Crown Point's offensive line, Summers is not easy to slow down, never mind stop.

"I will say our offensive line's pretty good," Buzea said. "When you can line up against those guys and say, 'Hey, we're running the ball,' and pop runs like that, they're doing something too. So let's give props to our offensive line."

Merrillville coach Brad Seiss also gave credit to Summers and Crown Point's offensive line.

"He's a big, physical runner," Seiss said. "They do a good job of getting good push up front. We had a lot of opportunities to get off the field, where he would just kind of show his strength and break tackles. He's a really good player."

So, too, is Hill, whose high school career ended with a memorable performance against the Bulldogs.

"Man, they have a great quarterback. … You don't see many like him," Buzea said. "He's very, very talented. He's AJ on their team, but in a different way."

Merrillville senior running back/slot receiver Cameron Jordan had 12 catches for 166 yards and three TDs, junior wide receiver Curtis Walker had 12 catches for 152 yards, and both of sophomore wide receiver William Golden's catches went for TDs as Hill deftly distributed the ball.

"We decided at halftime, we're just going to throw it every play and let our best player go to work, whether it's him throwing it in phase or using his legs to extend plays," Seiss said. "You just don't find many guys that can do the things that he does because most quarterbacks in high school, especially when they scramble, they scramble to run or they just totally look down and freak out.

"For him to have the composure he has to not only evade rushers and see down the field, he really showed crazy ability that second half, just kind of running around everywhere and finding open guys. He's a special talent. On top of that, he's a really good kid."

The Bulldogs, who advance to a sectional final on the road against Duneland Athletic Conference foe Lake Central (5-5), handed Merrillville its only two losses this season. The Pirates, who moved up to 6A this season, had won seven straight sectional titles, six regional titles during that stretch and broke through to reach the 5A state championship game last year.

"Shoutout Crown Point," Hill said. "I hope they take it all the way and put the Region on the map."

Crown Point's last loss to a Region team was a sectional opener against Merrillville in 2021, a game that ended Buzea's first season with the team.

"I have a ton of respect for Brad and his staff," Buzea said. "This was the type of football game you were supposed to have here. Unfortunately, it's not for a championship. That's a whole different thing if you want to sit down, have a conversation with me."

Now Jaeger and the Bulldogs can talk about trying to win a sectional title.

"I'm glad that I've been playing so good, but it's just really about the team and what we've been able to accomplish," Jaeger said. "I'm just glad I can contribute."

articles.title: ESPN projects Florida among college basketball’s 30-win teams
articles.summary: ESPN included Florida among 17 teams capable of reaching 30 wins, a mark no SEC program reached last season.
articles.body:
Florida basketball enters the season with national championship expectations, and ESPN believes the Gators have the roster to pile up wins along the way.

ESPN's Myron Medcalf included Florida among 17 teams he projects as candidates to reach 30 wins during the 2026-27 season. The Gators join Duke, Kansas, Illinois, Arizona, UConn and several other national contenders on the list.

Reaching 30 wins would be especially notable in the SEC. No team from the conference hit that mark last season, despite the league sending multiple teams to the NCAA Tournament and remaining one of the deepest conferences in the country.

Thirty wins have also become a useful benchmark for identifying teams capable of making a championship run. ESPN noted that eight of the past 11 national champions had already reached at least 28 wins by Selection Sunday.

Florida certainly has the talent to fit that profile.

PHOTOS: Top highlights from Florida's preseason win against Stetson

Medcalf pointed to the return of Denzel Aberdeen, who was part of Florida's 2025 national championship team before spending last season away from the program, as another piece of continuity for Todd Golden's roster.

He also offered perhaps the strongest endorsement possible of the Gators' personnel, calling Florida's group "the most talented roster in the country." Medcalf highlighted Thomas Haugh as a Wooden Award contender and Rueben Chinyelu and Alex Condon as All-SEC candidates.

Haugh, Chinyelu and Condon have already piled up preseason recognition. Haugh was named SEC Preseason Player of the Year, while he and Chinyelu earned first-team preseason All-SEC honors and Condon landed on the second team.

All three were also named to the 20-player preseason watch list for the NABC Division I Player of the Year, making Florida the only program with three selections.

Aberdeen's return could provide another boost. Medcalf reported that returning Florida players believe the veteran guard has helped restore chemistry that the team struggled to find last season.

ESPN's projections were reasonably accurate a year ago. Eight of the 11 teams that eventually reached 30 victories appeared on its preseason list, while the 17 teams ESPN picked averaged 27.9 wins.

Florida begins the season ranked No. 1 nationally and will get its first opportunity to justify those expectations Monday against No. 17 Miami in Tampa.

articles.title: Mekies dismisses Horner’s claim that Red Bull have lost team spirit
articles.summary: Laurent Mekies dismissed Christian Horner’s claim that Formula One team Red Bull have “lost their mojo” since his departure. The Frenchman replaced Horner at...
articles.body:
Laurent Mekies dismissed Christian Horner's claim that Formula One team Red Bull have "lost their mojo" since his departure.

The Frenchman replaced Horner at the helm of the team after the 52-year-old was sacked following a trophy-laden 20-year spell in charge in July last year.

Red Bull ensured a tough start to the season under the sport's new regulations, but have made strides forward in recent races, with Max Verstappen winning back-to-back rounds in Malaysia and Singapore.

As part of his recent book promotion, Horner claimed that the team vibe is not the same since he departed.

"Christian is entitled to his opinion. He obviously spent a lot of time in this team," Mekies said ahead of Sunday's race in Mexico City.

"I respect his point of view. We certainly feel extremely differently about the vibe in the team.

"I think one of the strong points we've been drawing on, certainly in the last few months, is the incredible team spirit that has allowed us to come back from an objectively very difficult moment.

"We certainly had a challenging first part of the year, chassis side and power unit side, and the way the team stuck together, the way the team set the Milton Keynes department on fire to try to come back, and the way they have done that… I think that's the Red Bull spirit."

Red Bull are using their own power trains for the first time this season, the culmination of a five-year project launched in 2021 and overseen by Horner until his departure.

Their engine has been ranked by the FIA as the best on the grid and the team are beginning to reap the reward.

Red Bull sit joint-third in the constructors' standings, locked on points with McLaren, but 252 points adrift of runaway leaders Mercedes.

While heartened by their progress, Mekies is determined to kick the team forward to being back in championship contention.

"It's always one thing to have a positive spirit when you are winning races. It's something else to have that same fighting spirit and unity between the team members when you are put under pressure," Mekies added.

"That's certainly how we feel we need to go racing. The guys got the rewards they deserved with the turnaround that they have produced, which is, I think, very remarkable.

"But, ultimately, we are well aware that we live and die with our results. The target is not to win one race or two races.

"The target is to be back to world titles and, until we are there, nobody will feel we have achieved anything."

articles.title: What to know about Luke Fahey, Ohio State football's true freshman QB
articles.summary: With Julian Sayin injured, true freshman Luke Fahey could make his first start for Ohio State against USC.
articles.body:
Luke Fahey made his debut for Ohio State football on Sept. 5, but the true freshman may be making his debut as a starter against USC on Oct 31.

Fahey replaced quarterback Julian Sayin during Ohio State's 19-15 win against Indiana on Oct. 17 after Sayin was sacked in the fourth quarter. Sayin exited to the locker room and appeared on the sideline later with a sling on his arm.

Fahey took Sayin's place for the final three offensive drives. He was 0-for-2 passing and logged minus-2 rushing yards, but the Buckeyes defense held on, helping OSU to win the top-five matchup.

Luke Fahey in action: Photos from 2026 Ohio State football season

Luke Fahey was ahead of fellow backup quarterback Tavien St. Clair before Julian Sayin's injury

At the beginning of preseason training camp, coach Ryan Day praised Fahey 's development.

"He's really been doing a great job," Day said in August. "He's putting a lot of pressure on Tavien. He really is. He's been competing. He's been making plays."

Before camp, it was presumed that St. Clair would move up after spending last year as the third-stringer. St. Clair stood out during the spring game in April. The Bellefontaine native was the first Ohio high school quarterback since Joe Burrow to sign a scholarship agreement with Ohio State, and he was a highly touted five-star prospect.

In the week leading up to Ohio State's season opener, Day said that St. Clair and Fahey would continue to split reps with the second-team offense in practices leading up to the game. By the time the Ball State game came around on Sept. 5, it was Fahey, not St. Clair, who entered the contest after Sayin's day was done.

Fahey took over with 7:17 remaining in the third quarter with Ohio State leading 42-3. After completing his first pass for two yards to Isaiah West, Fahey threw an interception after freshman wide receiver Chris Henry Jr. dropped the pass, which popped up for opposing cornerback Cedric Franklin III to grab.

Luke Fahey was a three-star quarterback in the 2026 class

Fahey was the No. 35 quarterback in the 2026 class, according to 247Sports' composite rankings. He quickly stepped up and lost his black stripe following the Buckeyes' first preseason intrasquad scrimmage on Aug. 15.

Luke Fahey split reps as a high school quarterback until his senior year

Fahey grew up in Southern California and went to Mission Viejo High School.

At Mission Viejo, Fahey played in a two-quarterback system with Draiden Trudeau for his sophomore and junior seasons. Trudeau ended up as a three-star recruit in the Class of 2025 and committed to play football at San Diego State.

"I feel God has a plan for everybody," Fahey told the Los Angeles Times ahead of his senior season in 2025. "That was my journey. Of course, everyone wants to be a full-time starter, but that was a good thing for me. There was a lot of adversity during those two years."

Fahey became the outright starter his senior year and had 7,021 passing yards, 68 passing touchdowns and nine interceptions through his high school career. Fahey was a multisport athlete, also playing lacrosse and basketball.

Luke Fahey is the shortest Ohio State quarterback this century

Fahey is listed at 5 feet 11 inches on the Ohio State website.

If Fahey starts against USC, he would be the shortest starting quarterback for the Buckeyes this century. Troy Smith is the shortest quarterback to make a start, and he was listed at 6 feet tall.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor trade talks are "active and ongoing"
articles.summary: Seahawks, Packers, Broncos, Vikings, Giants are pegged as potential destinations.
articles.body:
There are two ways to handle the trade of a cornerstone player. One, talk quietly to a minimal number of teams. Like the Titans did with defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Two, throw the doors open and try to get the best possible package of draft picks and/or players in return. Like the Colts are now doing with running back Jonathan Taylor.

Indianapolis has officially declared that Taylor is available , via a selective and strategic leak to ESPNFL. Trade talks are "active and ongoing," per the report.

The teams that have "expressed at least some level of interest" are the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, Giants, and Seahawks.

Last weekend's Sunday Splash! report that operated as the "everything must go" sign for the Colts pegged the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, and Seahawks as potentially interested teams in Taylor. The Giants (who are believed, we're told by multiple sources, to have been pursuing Simmons) are a new arrival. Which would possibly be bad news for second-year running back Cam Skattebo, who emerged from the doghouse last week with 124 rushing yards. (It wouldn't be a surprise if the Giants offered Skattebo to the Colts as part of the trade package, frankly.)

To the extent that tying four teams to the trade talks doesn't get the Colts maximum compensation, the new report notes that the Colts "would prefer" that Taylor stick around for their "rebuild."

If they really wanted Taylor, they wouldn't be fielding trade offers fo him.

The Colts reportedly are looking for a package similar to what the 49ers sent to the Panthers in 2022 for running back Christian McCaffrey: a second-round pick, a third-round pick, and a fourth-round pick in the 2023 draft and a fifth-round pick in the 2024 draft.

The next question is whether Taylor will play on Sunday. It's possible, in our view, the Colts will hold Taylor out of action on Sunday at Jacksonville, like the Cardinals did three weeks ago when they had a deal in place to trade receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans. Even without a deal, keeping Taylor out of the game would ensure that he won't get injured.

If that happens, rookie Seth McGowan would be the likely starter in Week 8. Last Sunday, the seventh-rounder who played for Kentucky last year had 11 carries for 48 yards in a 16-10 loss to the Vikings.

And the Vikings continue to make the most sense for Taylor. Especially since they had the best possible opportunity to scout him six days ago, when he had 18 carries for 95 yards and an Adrian Peterson-style 38-yard touchdown run.

If the Vikings add Taylor in the coming days, he'd likely make his debut as soon as next Monday night, when the Vikings host the Bills. And when they put Peterson in the team's Ring of Honor.

articles.body:
Texas A&M football fans can probably use a break for their favorite squad.

After a top-10 ranking early in the year and the return of several players who helped the Aggies to the College Football Playoff in 2025, this year hasn't gone great.

The 4-4 Aggies were an early victim to resurgent Kentucky football and suffered embarrassing setbacks LSU and Missouri. But A&M hosts Tennessee (6-2, 3-2 SEC) next month and could dash the Volunteers' postseason hopes with a win.

Then of course there's the biggest game on the calendar each year: A&M vs. Texas. Despite being just 1-4 in conference play so far, Aggies fans no doubt would love an opportunity to blow a hole in UT's season. A final-week A&M win could doom a Longhorns squad with little margin for error when it comes to the postseason.

But what about this Saturday? Is Texas A&M in action during Week 9? And what's the rest of the Aggies' schedule look like?

Nope. The Aggies have their lone "open week" or bye. Last week, the Aggies fell to Alabama on the road despite holding a lead. Next week, they'll play South Carolina.

articles.title: Johan Ghazali Runs It Back With Johan Estupinan At The Inner Circle 42 On December 11
articles.summary: "Jojo" and "Panda Kick" will finish what they started at Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand.
articles.body:
The explosive "Battle of the Johans" is officially set for its second chapter, as two of the flyweight division's most electrifying young strikers prepare to finish what they started.

Malaysian-American sensation Johan "Jojo" Ghazali and Colombian knockout artist Johan "Panda Kick" Estupinan meet again at The Inner Circle 42 on Friday, December 11, in a sequel to one of the most action-packed flyweight Muay Thai clashes in recent memory. The rematch goes down live in Asia primetime from Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, and streams exclusively for members at live.onefc.com .

For Ghazali, this rematch is personal. The 19-year-old comes in determined to avenge one of the toughest defeats of his young career and reclaim the momentum Estupinan took from him.

Ghazali stormed onto the scene with a blistering 6-1 promotional run, earning a coveted US$100,000 contract and capturing the imagination of fans worldwide. Armed with concussive power, natural swagger, and sharp microphone skills, "Jojo" has built a 28-11 career record that includes six highlight-reel promotional stoppages.

His rise stalled, however, when he collided with fellow phenom Estupinan at ONE 170 in January 2025. After Ghazali scored a first-round knockdown that had the fight firmly in his grasp, Estupinan floored him in return in round two, broke away in the final frame, and claimed a unanimous decision.

That defeat opened one of the most testing stretches of his promising career, as Ghazali went 3-3 against the division's top emerging talent.

Guided by ONE Featherweight Kickboxing World Champion Superbon , he has become sharper with each setback. That growth was on full display at The Inner Circle 35 this past October, as he settled his score with Diego Paez in arguably the most complete performance of his career.

With one rivalry resolved, Ghazali now turns his crosshairs to another.

Standing ready to turn back that revenge bid is Estupinan, who launched his promotional tenure with a stunning five-fight winning run. The 24-year-old brings a helter-skelter, salsa-infused striking rhythm to the ring, blending unorthodox angles, flying attacks, and pure showmanship to disrupt even the sharpest Muay Thai timing.

That run was punctuated by back-to-back US$50,000 performance bonuses before the victory over Ghazali thrust him firmly into the division's upper echelon.

Yet Estupinan soon encountered turbulence of his own. A competitive decision loss to Japanese tactician Taiki Naito and a second-round TKO defeat to Black Panther sparked questions regarding his defensive discipline and penchant for reckless firefights.

The JCFernandez and Team CSK representative answered those questions emphatically at his kickboxing debut at ONE Fight Night 44 this past June, delivering his most complete performance yet to snap the perfect promotional record of Akif "King" Guluzada by unanimous decision, lifting his overall record to 28-2. That kickboxing redemption had set the table for a rematch with Naito at ONE Fight Night 49, but an injury ruled him out of that card , so December 11 marks his return to Muay Thai.

Estupinan comes in determined to reassert his mastery over Ghazali, prove his striking supremacy, and put the rivalry to bed at 2-0.

Both warriors have been forged by their setbacks, and whoever has his hand raised on December 11 will stake a compelling claim for a berth in the top five of ONE's loaded flyweight Muay Thai division.

articles.title: Aston Villa to sue ex-Liverpool star Carragher over ‘unacceptable insults’
articles.summary: Aston Villa chairman accuses ex-Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher of insulting the club, with legal action threatened.
articles.body:
Aston Villa will pursue legal action ⁠against pundit Jamie ⁠Carragher, the Premier League club has said, accusing the former Liverpool defender of making “unacceptable insults” about the ⁠club and their supporters.

Villa’s response followed comments by Carragher on the Stick to Football podcast, where he told Villa ⁠supporters to “shut the [expletive] up” and said, “Aston Villa will never be Manchester United”, suggesting there is a hierarchy in football.

“I’m not trying to annoy Villa fans but there is a chain in football, whether you like it or not,” said Carragher. “So Real Madrid will take Man United’s best player, they’ll take [Cristiano] Ronaldo. There’s very few above United, the same with Liverpool.

“But there will be teams below Aston Villa and they [Villa] will take their manager or they will take their players, so shut the f*** up Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Man United.”

With Michael Carrick’s role at United in danger after the team’s dismal start to the season, Carragher also discussed speculation linking Villa manager Unai Emery with a move to Old Trafford should the opportunity arise.

“Aston Villa will initiate ‌legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans,” Villa chairman Nassef Sawiris said on Friday.

“Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football.”

The club did not say on what legal basis it would take action. It did not ⁠immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

The news agency added that Carragher ⁠did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Villa’s threat. He has sought to defuse the controversy, saying he made the remarks in jest.

“It ⁠was a joke after the stick Villa fans have given me over saying Emery ⁠may fancy joining Man Utd,” Carragher said ⁠on social media.

“I hope these clown clips show me praising Emery/Villa like I have done for years & saying how pleased I was you won [the 2026 Europa ‌League] in Istanbul.”

Carragher also reiterated that his comments reflected his high regard for Emery rather than any perceived shortcomings at ‌Villa, ‌saying he regarded the Spaniard as one of the best managers in the Premier League.

articles.title: Report: Jonathan Taylor trade talks 'active and ongoing' for Colts
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are "open to trading" star running back Jonathan Taylor, according to Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are "open to trading" star running back Jonathan Taylor, according to NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport.

This report differs from others that have been out there. Previously, reports stated that while trading Taylor was still a possibility, the Colts wanted to keep him on the team as a key part of the rebuild.

But now, the Colts seem ready to move on if the price is right.

Schefter adds that "multiple teams" have reached out to the Colts and those conversations are "active and ongoing."

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler added that Taylor could net the Colts a "second-round pick and more" in return.

Although Taylor just signed a two-year, $44 million contract extension prior to the season, the contract is movable if needed.

Taylor continues to be one of the most productive backs in football, totaling 587 yards with eight rushing touchdowns. He doesn't have a 100-yard game this season, but has hit the 90-yard mark in five of seven games.

articles.title: 11 best athlete Halloween costumes of 2026
articles.summary: From spooky transformations to clever pop culture tributes, check out the best athlete Halloween costumes of 2026
articles.body:
Halloween gives athletes another great excuse to show off their fun side. Stepping away from games and practices, stars swapped out their jerseys for outfits inspired by their favorite movies, TV shows, music and pop culture trends. Some went all out with heavy makeup and costumes, while others went for quick, funny looks that got a good laugh.

Team parties brought some of the best moments. The Detroit Lions showed up dressed as classic movie characters and musicians, while the San Francisco 49ers got creative at a bye-week get-together hosted by Brock Purdy and his wife, Jenna. Even retired stars got in on the action, including a well-known couple who dressed up as another famous pair.

A great costume doesn't always need to be super fancy. Some hit the mark because the details were just right, while others were simply fun to see because of who was wearing them. Knowing how well these players are doing in their actual seasons made the looks even better.

Here are 11 of the best athlete Halloween costumes from 2026.

11. Brayden Willis & Tatyanah Bass as Mermaid Man & Barnacle Boy

San Francisco 49ers tight end Brayden Willis and his girlfriend, Tatyanah Bass, picked two familiar characters from "SpongeBob SquarePants." They dressed as Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy, the older superhero duo from the popular animated series.

Their costumes were part of the 49ers' Halloween party hosted by the Purdys. Bass shared videos from the gathering on her TikTok account, which has more than one million followers. Her posts gave fans a look at the players enjoying their time away from football.

The timing worked well for San Francisco. The 49ers were on their bye week after suffering their first loss of the season in Week 7. The gathering gave the team an opportunity to relax and spend time together before returning to the field.

Former tennis star Genie Bouchard went with a famous pop-culture look for Halloween 2026. She re-created Britney Spears' outfit from her memorable 2001 MTV Video Music Awards performance.

Bouchard completed the look with a fake python wrapped around her shoulders. The snake was an important part of Spears' original performance, making it a clear reference for fans who remember the iconic moment.

Although Bouchard has stepped away from professional tennis, she remains active on social media. Her costume brought back memories of one of the most recognizable performances in MTV awards history. The nostalgic tribute also showed her interest in pop culture beyond the tennis court.

9. Brock & Jenna Purdy as Sulley & Mike Wazowski

The San Francisco 49ers quarterback and his wife hosted the team's Halloween party in 2026. The couple dressed as Sulley and Mike Wazowski from Pixar's "Monsters, Inc."

Purdy took on the role of Sulley, the large blue monster, while Jenna dressed as the small green Mike Wazowski. Their costumes brought two of the film's most recognizable characters to the gathering.

The party took place during San Francisco's bye week. Purdy used the time to host a relaxed gathering and bring teammates together away from football.

San Francisco 49ers cornerback Nate Hobbs delivered one of the most unusual costumes of the season. He dressed as Daejon Love, the man accused of impersonating a professional football player online. Hobbs wore a Love jersey at the team's Halloween party.

TSN Sports shared the clip on X. Bass documented the party on her popular TikTok account, which has around 1 million followers.

Love's story gave the costume its unusual context. He was arrested before the season began and is accused of defrauding dozens of women of $1.3 million. He allegedly used a false professional football identity to gain their trust. Netflix is also planning a documentary titled "Wide Deceiver" about the case.

7. Caroline Wozniacki & David Lee as Taylor Swift & Travis Kelce

Retired tennis star Caroline Wozniacki and her husband, former NBA player David Lee, chose a celebrity-inspired couples costume. They dressed as singer Taylor Swift and Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce.

Wozniacki wore a blonde wig, a short dress, boots and a microphone accessory. Lee completed the look in a Chiefs uniform associated with Kelce. Their outfits offered a clear nod to one of the most talked-about celebrity couples in sports and entertainment.

Wozniacki shared photos on social media and tagged Swift. She also asked followers what they thought of the costumes.

The pair got an early start on Halloween and picked a costume that many fans could recognize immediately. Their outfits also connected two worlds that Wozniacki and Lee know well, professional sports and celebrity culture.

6. Amon-Ra St. Brown as old-school rapper

Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown went with a simple throwback look. He dressed like a 1990s rapper, wearing a red bandana, fitted cap and dark sunglasses.

The outfit relied on familiar hip-hop fashion rather than a detailed character transformation. Its simplicity made it a good fit for a team Halloween party.

St. Brown entered the season as one of Detroit's leading offensive players. The four-time Pro Bowler was listed with a rest designation on the Lions' Week 8 injury report. That allowed him to manage physical wear while remaining an important part of the team's plans.

St. Brown's costume was among the more relaxed looks from a Lions group that included several players in the celebrations.

Niners wide receiver Ricky Pearsall chose the International Man of Mystery for his Halloween costume. He dressed as Austin Powers, the fictional spy made famous by Mike Myers.

Pearsall's outfit re-created the character's recognizable style. The choice brought some comedy to the 49ers' internal Halloween gathering, where several players and their partners showed off their costumes.

Sports media praised Pearsall's look as one of the better outfits at the event. However, his season has been disrupted by an injury.

His costume offered a lighter moment during a difficult campaign. It also showed that players can make an impression at team events even when they are not available on the field.

4. Nick Bosa & Ella Ailiff as The Crimson Chin & Cleft the Boy Chin Wonder

San Francisco defensive end Nick Bosa and his girlfriend, Ella Ailiff, went with a cartoon-inspired costume. Their look was based on The Crimson Chin and Cleft the Boy Chin Wonder, superheroes associated with Timmy Turner in "The Fairly OddParents."

The costume featured the character's superhero mask and cape. Ailiff revealed the outfits in a TikTok video, showing the couple embracing the animated theme instead of choosing a traditional horror look.

3. Jared Goff & Christen Goff as Bobby Boucher & Vicki Vallencourt

Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff and his wife, Christen, re-created a couple from the 1998 sports comedy "The Waterboy." Goff dressed as Bobby Boucher, the fictional football player portrayed by Adam Sandler. Christen took on the role of Vicki Vallencourt.

Goff wore the orange and blue SCLSU Mud Dogs football uniform. Christen completed her outfit with a red crop top and cap, matching the character's familiar style from the film.

The choice was a natural fit for an NFL quarterback. "The Waterboy" remains a recognizable sports comedy, and its main character gives the costume a clear football connection.

Detroit running back Jahmyr Gibbs paid tribute to Michael Jackson at the Lions' Halloween party. He wore a sparkling blue jacket, dark sunglasses and a curly wig inspired by the pop star's 1980s appearance.

The outfit was easy to identify and brought a music legend into the team's celebrations. His costume paired a recognizable pop-culture tribute with strong recent numbers on the field.

1. Karl-Anthony Towns & Jordyn Woods as Night King & White Walker

Karl-Anthony Towns and his wife, Jordyn Woods, delivered one of the most detailed athlete Halloween looks of 2026. The New York Knicks center transformed into the Night King from "Game of Thrones" , while Woods dressed as a White Walker.

The couple debuted their outfits at a restaurant on Prince Street in SoHo, N.Y. Towns used heavy prosthetics to recreate the Night King's icy appearance. Woods matched him with a similarly chilling look. Costume designer Sabrina Spanta and special-effects makeup artist Roger Baena worked on the transformation, which included frostbite-inspired makeup and piercing blue eyes.

The outfits drew attention from HBO's official social media accounts, which called them the coldest couple in New York. Towns is also a known "Game of Thrones" fan. In April 2026, he joked to actor Kit Harington that he would bend the knee if his own knee did not hurt.

articles.title: Kubs maul Notus Pirates in postseason football play
articles.summary: Oct. 31—KAMIAH — Looking at Idaho Class 2A MaxPreps.com football rankings, which govern the state's postseason, one might have expected an evenly matched epi...
articles.body:
Oct. 31—KAMIAH — Looking at Idaho Class 2A MaxPreps.com football rankings, which govern the state's postseason, one might have expected an evenly matched epic as the Kamiah Kubs hosted the Notus Pirates in a state tournament game Friday at Bob Squires Sports Complex.

That expectation would have been utterly inaccurate. Eighth-ranked Kamiah, which stood above ninth-ranked Notus by the very barest of margins in the computerized system, was head-and-shoulders the better team on the field, reeling off the game's first four touchdowns within the opening quarter alone en route to a 34-14 victory.

"Our kids just knew what kind of team we were," Kamiah coach Garrison Bretz said. "They just had to execute and play physical, and that's just what we did."

The dynamic duo of Lawson Landmark and Todd Roberts took turns at quarterback and passed to each other for two touchdowns, factored in four of the team's five scoring plays and combined for 16 tackles on defense to lead the way as the Kubs produced the statement result.

"I think we just proved that the North does it better," Landmark said.

After a 2-3 start to their season, the Kubs have now won four straight contests. They will next await word on the opponent and location for an Idaho Class 2A state playoff quarterfinal as results and rankings shake out over the weekend.

In an early sign of the defensive dominance that would characterize Kamiah's outing, Devin Davis logged the game's first points on an end zone fumble recovery. Logan Keen went on to clinch the first offensive touchdown for the Kubs (6-3), squeezing down the right side of the field following a pass from Roberts for a 30-yard play.

Next up came a rare occurrence for back-to-back scoring plays: Landmark hit Roberts for a passing touchdown, then Roberts promptly returned the favor as the pair swapped positions from receiver to quarterback and vice versa, then back again.

Here are the circumstances behind the Kubs' unusual decision to swap quarterbacks twice within the first 12 minutes of play:

Landmark, formerly the Kamiah's starting quarterback, had stepped away from the position due to a wrist injury early this season, letting Roberts take over while he played receiver. Now that Landmark has recovered and Roberts has proven himself at QB, the two are sharing the slot.

"We kind of switch out because he earned his right to keep playing quarterback," Landmark said of Roberts. "I did miss it, but I do like wide receiver a lot."

With Landmark and Roberts' 1-2 punch capping things off, the Kubs were up 28-0 before the second quarter began.

The Kubs cooled down offensively after the opening quarter, but continued to utterly stymie any attempt by the Pirates (6-3) to answer their early onslaught. The game was into its final frame before Notus finally broke its scoring duck on a short running touchdown punched in by Sawyer Nicoletti.

Landmark would respond with about three-and-a-half minutes to go in regulation, cutting laterally to his left to evade the Notus line for a 6-yard scoring rush. Moments later, the boom of something like celebratory cannonfire issued from a balcony labeled "Go Kubs! End Zone Club."

The Pirates quickly found their second touchdown on the ensuing possession, but by then the game's outcome was essentially decided.

After the clock ran out with their final drive sitting at midfield, the Kubs assembled in front of the bleachers and serenaded their home fans with a recitation of the school's fight song:

"Come on Kamiah; fight-fight-fight! We'll always be winning our ballgames!

Come on Kamiah; win-win-win! Our Kub pack will carry us to fame!"

Roberts wrapped up the day passing 5-for-8 for 95 yards and two touchdowns, added eight carries and 60 yards on the ground and racked up seven tackles and a fumble recovery on defense.

Landmark added one TD apiece passing and rushing, went 4-for-8 passing for 54 yards and logged nine carries for 44 rushing yards on offense. He also had nine tackles, two fumble recoveries and an interception on defense.

Keen led the Kubs in rushing yards with 94 on 11 carries and added a receiving touchdown to his ledger, while Gatlin Griffith notched a team-high two sacks among his five tackles.

Coming into this game, Kamiah's total of 60.14 MaxPreps ranking points relative to Notus' 56.92 would not have suggested a blowout was in the offing, but the belief at Kamiah is that the records are somewhat deceiving this fall.

"As the season's moved on, we got a lot better," said Roberts, noting that factors like Landmark's injury hampered the Kubs' early performance. "I think people were not expecting us to be as good as we are. The North has some good competition; I think it's a lot tougher up here than down south.

"Excited for our next matchup," he added. "Hopefully we play in one of the domes."

What to look forward to in the upcoming playoffs? Bretz acknowledged that teams like favored Hagerman and Prairie of Cottonwood will pose formidable challenges, but maintains that his Kubs can hold their own against any of them.

"In the playoffs, it's anybody's ballgame," he said. "The records in the regular season don't matter in the playoffs. We've just got to go in with the mentality that we're good enough to play with these teams, we're good enough to beat these teams and see what happens."

articles.title: Northview rally falls short
articles.summary: After coming back from 17 down in the first half, Northview's high school football team couldn't come back from 17 down again in the second half as the Knigh...
articles.body:
After coming back from 17 down in the first half, Northview's high school football team couldn't come back from 17 down again in the second half as the Knights fell 38-31 at Indianapolis Chatard in a Class 4A sectional semifinal game Friday night.

Chatard went up 17-0 in the first quarter thanks to Harrison Odom throwing a 12-yard pass to Julio Graves to get the offense started before Brody Langlois kicked a field goal and Danny Adams added a touchdown.

Northview coach Mark Raetz said when the Knights got down 17 in the first quarter, they could've folded, and the same thing in the second half.

"But they fought back every time in spite of some stuff not going our way," Raetz said. "I'm just proud of the way they competed."

Raetz said the Knights were able to capitalize on some opportunities and gave his coaching staff props as well putting in some new wrinkles to the offense. He said Mike Bath, who coaches Northview's girls flag football team, gave the coaching staff some new ideas and that the players executed them pretty well.

The Knights answered with 21 unanswered points in the second quarter. The scoring spree was started by Jake Raetz rushing for four yards before he had another two-yard touchdown run. Then came an explosive 67-yard run from Cooper Schimmel as he found holes in the Chatard defense and hauled into the end zone.

Unfortunately for Northview, the Trojans took the lead back going into the locker room with a Hail Mary play, Odom launching a 41-yard pass to Cam Harden. That left the score 24-21 Chatard at the half.

Then the Trojans did in the second half what they did in the first half, 14 points in the third quarter much to the dismay of the many Northview fans who traveled. But the Knights put 10 points on the board in the fourth, starting with a trick play from Bryer McCluskey to Cooper Schimmel for 16 yards and a touchdown. After that, Lucas Whitman knocked in a 43-yard field goal to pull the Knights within seven with 6:41 left in the game.

Northview got the ball back, but the Chatard defense kept the Knights from tying or taking the lead.

Raetz said he thought his team competed hard and just had some breaks go against the Knights, especially at the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half.

"Our kids compete hard, they care," Raetz said. "It stinks."

Raetz gave props to the Trojans saying how they're a good team that leaves a small margin for error.

"We gave up a few touchdowns on jump balls. We knew their receivers were good, but at the same time you have to be able to hold up in the run game," Raetz said. "At times we got isolated man coverage and they made us pay a couple times."
